results.content:
Reading our release notes in another browser?

Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

# Dia got faster

You told us Dia was feeling sluggish, and you were right. So, we’ve released a series of thoughtful improvements that make everything feel lighter (and faster). You should already feel some of this, but we’re not finished just yet.

Here’s what we’ve done so far:

No more slowing down over time

Keep your Dia open for days, and it might start lagging. Or at least, it used to thanks to memory leaks. We found a few places where memory wasn’t being released properly—plus a platform bug that kept some views around after switching tabs. In some cases, that added up to gigabytes of extra memory.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/540c0f3a5c69c9377656c844783b7e3098aee058-1202x786.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/95a911aaf8ca67b59abc5f6a562429d9957e0dd8-1202x442.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Now that's fixed, Dia should feel more speedy (even if you rarely restart your laptop 👀).

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/64db6ed1fff0a6875fa2b72cd9d003f5150cbfc8-678x853.png)

Enhanced by

Seb, Brahm & Renato

Some smaller things that were adding up

#1

Animations on the new tab page now use fewer resources. We tuned when they run to reduce CPU and GPU usage — small savings that add up, especially when other tabs are busy.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/388339d9fe6150e6b37152038509b4dc8ccb9184-478x488.png)

Fixed by

Brahm and Adam

#2

The command bar is faster. By moving work out of the suggestion path and warming up favicon and database caches at startup, results show up more quickly as you type.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/4f69ff3c1982c9d3d100209cf169e488f2be475a-510x502.png)

Improved by

Renato

#3

And now, if your system is under load, we skip the extra step that decides whether input goes to search or Dia—saving resources when your machine needs it.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/4f69ff3c1982c9d3d100209cf169e488f2be475a-510x502.png)

Optimized by

Renato

The work doesn't stop there

The best way to help us keep improving Dia is by [joining our **Early Birds program**](https://www.diabrowser.com/earlybirds). When you join Early Birds, you’ll get early access to new features and fixes—and you’ll also get a direct line to provide us feedback on your experience.

If you hit a performance issue

Go to Help → Record a Performance Issue.

**Pro tip:** Include a description of what feels off and make sure the issue actually happens while you're recording ,so we capture it (and fix it)!

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/030f5e33615c337543e4637680b2f294b2c09879-1200x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

You can also tweet your feedback to us [@diabrowser](https://x.com/diabrowser). Speaking of, we’d like to shout out **@qbmgabriel** and **@alymoursy**. They didn’t just report performance issues but followed up with videos, tested our fixes, and helped us validate that things were actually getting better. That’s the type of collaboration we love here at BCNY.

**That’s it for this week.**

If something feels better, we’re glad. If something still feels off, tell us! We’re always trying to make Dia better (and faster), and you’re a big part of that.

### OneLastThing

My favorite working filmmaker [Radu Jude](https://letterboxd.com/director/radu-jude/)’s new movie _[Kontinental ‘25](https://letterboxd.com/film/kontinental-25/)_ is getting released in the US this Friday, so I've been thinking about his previous _[Do Not Expect Too Much From the End of the World](https://letterboxd.com/film/do-not-expect-too-much-from-the-end-of-the-world/)_ a lot this week. Riotously funny & also deeply morbid, it’s like the Romanian _Ulysses_. There’s a quote from him I keep coming back to — about [how in things that seem obsolete, “you discover that you can reinterpret them in a new context and they look much more modern.”](https://www.rogerebert.com/interviews/radu-jude-interview) I'm always looking for inspiration in the overlooked & forgotten as well.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/a10a944a0564fcfd3f910df353baf33fd90aefc9-496x500.png)

Praised by

Naman

Do Not Expect Too Much From the End of the World

Radu Jude

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/8ef8845e32516525a90d3b86aecd4ac023a7d622-1000x1481.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

results.content:
Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

# Your work comes to you

You’re in a meeting, and someone asks, “did you see the doc I shared?” You didn’t.

We’ve all been there: a comment you missed, a page you never saw, a doc you made weeks ago that’s suddenly back in play.

What if you didn’t have to go looking for that work at all? What if it came to you?

We started with GitHub, but today, Live Work goes beyond code.

Introducing Live Docs

**Live Docs** is a new Live Tab Group that surfaces your active Notion pages and Google Docs in one place. **Live Docs** pulls in comments, suggestions, mentions—all the “hey, can you look at this?” moments—and brings them to you. One group, no tab wrangling.

Jump in, then move on

Your docs appear when there’s activity, like a comment, a mention, or a share. Plus, they link straight to the change, not the top of the page so you can jump right in. Once you’ve handled it, the doc fades out. Clear the last one, and your group goes quiet. That empty state? You earned it.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/def109532b4acd0c5baf6cb1ba9e4804b6eb0539-1496x998.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Know when your work is landing

When your doc starts getting traction, _you’ll know_. **Live Docs** shows viewer counts on shared pages—so when your proposal has “5 viewers today,” you know it’s making the rounds.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1a5d43501ba6f1c138a8a9950c88d614a2b20692-882x588.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

**Live Work is expanding**

With GitHub, we brought live work to engineers. With **Live Docs**, we’re bringing it to everyone whose work lives in documents.

Your work comes to you, stays in your line of sight while it matters, and cleans up when it’s done.

### OneLastThing

I took photography classes in high school and recently decided to get back into it! I purchased [a refurbished Pentax K1000](https://cute.camera/) film camera and have been having a lot of fun testing out different film. I normally take digital photos, but film really makes you pick your shot, and it has been really refreshing. I recently took a bunch of photos while traveling in Kauai; the one here is of the Napali Coast!

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1ce371d9424f3025722e0d0a99a317ce7b3f9bfb-1120x1108.png)

Snapped by

Molly

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/e9eccfec1250dc7f1b6cc3a57a5e8b2e7eceb0eb-3017x2000.jpg?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

results.content:
Reading our release notes in another browser?

Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

# Onboarding without tab overload

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/6649fdec921707ab7c9654a0c32b282fb91f51f2-512x512.jpg?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

from the desk of

**Dustin, Head of Design**

Lately, I’m most excited about how our tab management story has evolved. We’ve gone from users having little to no organization (and asking for it) to being able to organize in ways that match their own complexity. A lot of this power isn’t pushed—features like pinning are there if you want to reach for them. It feels easier to pick up than what we did in Arc, because it grows with you instead of being forced upfront.

We’ve got a bunch of people joining us in the coming weeks—here's how they might get started using our latest release.

Dia from Day One

Day One

On your first day at The Browser Company, you get an onboarding doc, filled with things to know, down to the WiFi password for the office.

⌘ **-Click** when you open links from the onboarding doc to automatically get a new tab group with that doc, and all the links you open from it. Every relevant link for will be together in one place.

Day Two

You’re in a meeting with your manager, and want to show up prepared. You can now **Pin a Tab Group** to keep it in one spot, no matter how many tabs you open. Pinned groups sync across all windows within each profile, and persist even if you close a window or restart Dia, so you’ll always know where Onboarding is.

Day Three

You’re starting to write up strategy, but need to reference some materials you saw earlier in the week. Just attach the Onboarding Tab Group to any chat, and ask for what you need. **Attaching a Tab Group** brings more context from your tabs into Chat, getting you answers fast.

Day Four

You’ve made it through your first week, and you’re starting to get the hang of things. **Close out** by click the X of the Tab Group. You can always find it again in the recently closed menu or History.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/6f58fa4fa7feb27143fed3f5c3edd362e23dadb6-1200x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Also important—we've added **Tab panel in Settings**. Our defaults are strong, but opt out if something doesn’t work for you. And you can always change once you’re onboarded.

We’re ending support for Manifest V2 extensions.

Starting in next week's release, 1.17, Dia will stop supporting Manifest V2 extensions. Any V2 extensions you’ve installed will stop working and display a “no longer supported” message.

Dia’s built‑in ad blocker remains on by default, and most popular extensions update to Manifest V3 automatically. This brings Dia in line with other Chromium‑based browsers and removes reliance on deprecated, less secure code paths.

results.content:
Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

# Organize your Tabs

A few tabs, a busy work day, and your browser can start to feel unruly. To be honest, Dia hasn’t really helped here yet… but that changes today.

This release is our first step toward making Dia your own—with a new tool that brings order and makes your surface truly yours. It may look familiar, but it works in a way that’s unmistakably Dia.

Introducing Tab Groups

You can now group your tabs. By project, by initiative, or however you organize your work.

Whether you’re in the sidebar or the top bar, right click on a tab and move it into a new group. Add and remove tabs from your group with a drag or a click, and quickly collapse or expand it to keep your tab strip tidy.

You can customize each Tab Group with a color and an emoji or icon. When you hover over your tab group, you get a preview of what’s inside the group, and you can always select a tab from there.

When you close a Tab Group, it will automatically move to your bookmark bar as a little “storage” space for your groups. From there, you can relaunch a group anytime—or ⌘ + click to open it in a new window.

Group together the top of mind tabs that you really, really need to have organized. This could be onboarding documentation for your two new hires. Or a GTM initiative with a Figma file, strategy memo, and meeting notes. Or, of course, gift ideas for your office White Elephant party (might we suggest the MoMa store and a pair of socks).

A few more updates

- **More New Commands.** Following last week’s release, the feedback was clear—more commands, please! Create so much more “new” right from the command bar, like blog, wiki, and jira.

_Added by Nathan Chapman._
- **Book your Resy (and more).** There was a bug where Resy sometimes would not load correctly. We've fixed that so you can get back to booking your reservations.

_Fixed by Seb Marchand._

### OneLastThing

While making the images for this week’s notes, I multitasked at my holiday shopping. High on the list: these red Esmé socks I've heard amazing things about. I used to think socks were a boring gift, now they're basically all I want.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/5b00f9bb0354a387895d9a997a8a4e35e8a6ff37-400x400.png)

results.content:
Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

Reading our release notes in another browser?

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/1573bb536e39c579201cbc00b80864007e464456-71x71.png?w=60)Try Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/download "Try Dia")

# Stop opening PRs blind

You know that feeling. A PR lands in your queue… and before you even open it, you're covering your eyes. Is it three lines or three hundred? Did CI pass? Is there a merge conflict hiding in there?

Now you can tell before you click. Hover over your PRs in your Github Live Group and Dia shows you CI status and any merge conflicts so you can get a rough read on how big the diff is. Open the ones that need you. Ignore the ones that don't (we didn’t officially say this).

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/bac57e7f072ad43882d6c0b57ebcc4f33831b620-512x512.jpg)

Shipped by

Vardhan

### Offtheclock

My 2026 goal was to needlepoint Christmas stockings for me and my fiancé. After finding out finishing delays can take up to 5 months, I’ve been on the clock to finish these by end of May to have them back before Christmas. Clock is on, but they're almost done!

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/641700d497a0504b2ccfe38ae71efa6842896fc7-512x512.png)

Crafted by

Clare Bergman

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/2eaed38e96fcae57daa12956f7ccd21b88377e26-4257x4141.jpg?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

A few more updates

**Confluence joins the table.** Confluence is now supported in Live Groups, so you can see the Confluences docs that need your attention alongside Notion and Gmail in your Docs Live Group.

_Shipped by Vardhan Mudunuru_

**One emoji to rule them all.** Tab groups now get an automatically selected emoji that represents what’s inside, making them easier to scan and recognize at a glance.

_Shipped by Philip Massey_

**Dia checks Notion now, too.** Notion mentions, comment threads, and share invites all surface in chat, so it’s easier to stay caught up without context switching.

_Shipped by Ali Juma_

Want early access to features like these? [Join our Early Birds program](https://form.typeform.com/to/ukTpVjIv?typeform-source=browserco.typeform.com).
